chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Had Gadya, Further Thoughts
chapters.title: Further Thoughts

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Had Gadya, Further Thoughts:1
textUnits.text: Having earlier expressed the Jewish hope, “Next year in Jerusalem,” we end our Seder night with the universal hope that the Angel of Death will one day be defeated by the long-overdue realisation that God is life; that worshipping God means sanctifying life; that God’s greatest command is “Choose life” (Devarim 30:19); that we bring God into the world by reciting a blessing over life.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Had Gadya, Further Thoughts:2
textUnits.text: I find it almost unbearably moving that a people that has known so much suffering can summon the moral courage to end this evening of Jewish history on a supreme note of hope, and write it into the hearts of its children in the form of a nursery rhyme, a song. For what we give our children on this night of nights is something more and greater than the bread of oppression and the taste of Jewish tears. It is a faith that in this world, with all its violence and cruelty, we can create moments of redemption, signals of transcendence, acts of transfiguring grace. No people has risked and suffered more for a more slender hope, but no hope has lifted a people higher and led it, time and again, to greatness. So we end the night with a prayer and a conviction. The prayer: “God of life, help us win a victory over the forces of death.” And the conviction? That by refusing to accept the world that is, together we can start to make the world that ought to be.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.text: 3. How does this song connect to our lives today?

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Had Gadya, Experiencing the Seder
chapters.title: Experiencing the Seder

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Had Gadya, Experiencing the Seder:1
textUnits.text: Ask every person at your Seder table in turn to share what their hopes for the next year are: hopes for themselves, for the Jewish people, and for the world.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions
chapters.title: Educational Companion to the Questions

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:1
textUnits.text: HA LAḤMA ANYA
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:2
textUnits.text: As Rabbi Sacks explains in his Haggada, the root of the word “haggada” means not only “to tell” but also “to bind,” and the Seder evening binds us together as a people. Jews from all walks of life and religious backgrounds will find themselves at a Seder table, and should be welcomed. In fact, the biblical command to sacrifice the Pesaḥ lamb had to be done in a Ḥavura, which is more than one family coming together. The Exodus freedom is not just about leaving slavery, but also about journeying to the Promised Land and building a society based on the values of the Torah, where kindness to strangers will be a core value. This starts tonight.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:3
textUnits.text: The beauty of matza is that it can represent both. In fact, without slavery we would not appreciate our freedom, so both concepts can exist in this experience at the same time.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:4
textUnits.text: Although some families choose to have Seder night on their own (especially if they have young children, so the parents can focus on them) and this is perfectly okay, most people will find themselves at a Seder night with others from outside of their immediate family. People come together for this ritual. But more than this, it is a powerful thought that the entire Jewish people find themselves at a Seder table at the same time, and with some imagination, we can also feel connected to the generations that went before us who celebrated this festival in exactly the same way.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:5
textUnits.text: MA NISHTANA
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:6
textUnits.text: Learning through questions makes the educational process engaging and empowering for the learner.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:7
textUnits.text: Any question asked out of a desire for knowledge, without a secondary agenda, is a good question. There are no bad questions in this case.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:8
textUnits.text: Not all questions have answers, or at least answers that humans with finite and limited understanding can arrive at. Some questions only the infinite God can answer. But we don’t stop asking the questions. The questions are more important than the answers.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:9
textUnits.text: AVADIM HAYINU
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:10
textUnits.text: As a nation, we have a national memory and identity. So when the Haggada speaks of our experience in Egypt as slaves, while this refers to a specific generation and historical time period, as a nation we have that experience implanted in our national memory and identity. The Haggada encourages us to re-experience this every year on Seder night, and Avadim Hayinu reminds us that the experience does impact us directly, for if God had not redeemed us, we would be slaves ourselves to this day.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:11
textUnits.text: A good story told well can have a big impact. Stories can be powerful when they are experiential, in that the listener can imagine that they are living the story, or at least empathise and identify with the characters and their experiences. The longer and more detailed the story is, the better the chances are that this will happen. So the Haggada encourages us to tell the story at length, and deeply engage with it, so we can experience the story as fully as possible.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:12
textUnits.text: Because Seder night is not about “learning” or “reading” or “understanding” but rather about experiencing and living the story, the Haggada tells us that even wise and experienced people who have done this many times before still have to retell the story. Each year it is a new experience.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:13
textUnits.text: THE FOUR CHILDREN
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:14
textUnits.text: Obviously all answers are legitimate, but in the ensuing discussion it is worth encouraging everyone to realise that each of us is all of the four children at different times in our lives (or even at different times of the day!).
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:15
textUnits.text: All children are different and have different educational needs. Insightful parents and teachers realise this and try their hardest to cater to those individual needs.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:16
textUnits.text: Children are the main focus of the evening because this night more than any other is when we pass on our national heritage to the next generation. Even though the process of learning about and re-experiencing the Exodus is a task which takes a lifetime, it begins when we are children, laying the foundation of our Jewish identity and allowing the national narrative to become part of our very core. We take our cue from the Torah itself, which focuses on the questions children will ask about the Exodus.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:17
textUnits.text: THE TEN PLAGUES
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:18
textUnits.text: Each plague attacked a different aspect of the physical and spiritual needs of Egyptian society. The Egyptians could probably have managed without one or two or even more of the elements that were attacked, but all ten plagues together was a systematic destruction of their way of life.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:19
textUnits.text: Every plague was terrible and designed to attack a different aspect of Egyptian society and cause problems for the Egyptians. If you have to choose one…it doesn’t get more terrible than the final plague.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:20
textUnits.text: God could have taken the Israelites out of Egypt without any miracles or drama. But He chose to take the Egyptians on an educational journey, because the process was important. And even more important than the direct impact on the Egyptians was the impact on the world that was watching (or at least hearing reports) and the effect on the Israelites themselves. The plagues were as much for these other groups as they were for Pharaoh and the Egyptians, if not more so.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:21
textUnits.text: DAYEINU
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:22
textUnits.text: Full redemption from Egypt was the establishing of a sovereign nation in the Promised Land, with the Temple at the centre of its religious and political life. If God had stopped short of this at any of the previous stages, then it would not have been complete redemption.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:23
textUnits.text: The message behind Dayeinu is that each individual stage was miraculous and magnificent, and worthy of praise and gratitude.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:24
textUnits.text: While the physical redemption ended with the liberation from slavery and leaving the geographical boundaries of Egypt, and the spiritual redemption took place at the Giving of the Torah on Sinai, the full religio-social redemption was only achieved once the Jews entered the land of Israel and built a society there based on the Torah.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:25
textUnits.text: PESAḤ, MATZA, MAROR
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:26
textUnits.text: It is experiential. We don’t just talk or learn or read about the story, we experience it through food and other rituals (such as leaning, pouring for each other, etc.) in order to relive the story.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:27
textUnits.text: Yes, all the Ḥagim in Judaism do, although to a lesser extent than Pesaḥ. For example, we sit in the sukka, and we stay up all night learning to prepare to receive the Torah on Shavuot.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:28
textUnits.text: While some of our educational institutions do practise experiential education (camp is the best example) and some of our schools find opportunities to also do so (such as by having shabbatonim), perhaps institutions of formal Jewish education could find more creative ways to incorporate the methodology of experiential education.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:29
textUnits.text: HALLEL
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:30
textUnits.text: It is hard to know where to start. But it is important to articulate all the things God did for the Israelites and how we benefit from these acts until this day. In the words of the Haggada itself, “And if the Holy One, blessed be He, had not brought our fathers out of Egypt – then we, and our children, and the children of our children, would still be enslaved to Pharaoh in Egypt.”
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:31
textUnits.text: If one is comfortable finding words that articulate genuine emotion, then there is room for that in our prayers. But for many this is a challenge, and so we fall back on the exquisite words of our greatest poets and spiritual leaders, to give us the words we need. Our challenge is then to channel our emotions through these words.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:32
textUnits.text: For some, words capture the feelings and emotions that we need to express. But for others, only music can connect to our soul to do this sufficiently. While Rabbi Sacks was a masterful wordsmith and orator, he acknowledged that music can take us further along when it comes to expressing what is in our soul.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:33
textUnits.text: NIRTZA
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:34
textUnits.text: They should (and do) because this section refers to a rebuilt Jerusalem in Messianic times, when the Temple will exist (allowing us to celebrate Pesaḥ as originally described in the Torah) in a redeemed world of peace. This has clearly not been achieved yet, and so it is appropriate to pray for this at the end of the Seder night, even while sitting in the beautiful rebuilt modern city of Jerusalem.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:35
textUnits.text: The Exodus is the beginning of a journey that we are still on. The destination of this journey is rebuilt Jerusalem in a redeemed world of peace. We hope that this can be achieved in time for next year’s Seder.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:36
textUnits.text: All the Ḥagim are special and unique in Israel. There is something very powerful about celebrating a Jewish festival in a Jewish state. It is also easier to remember that we are closer to the final destination of the Jewish journey now than at any point in history, when sitting in the ancient Jewish homeland, rebuilt in modern times.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:37
textUnits.text: ḤAD GADYA
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:38
textUnits.text: The whole of the Seder is focused on children, and on transmitting our heritage to the next generation. Like the other songs at the conclusion of the Seder, this song is fun to sing, and it also contains a strong educational message. This is a great way to end the Seder night journey.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:39
textUnits.text: The message of Ḥad Gadya is that while it may seem during our history that there are powerful forces who will dominate and even destroy us, these forces come and go, and only God decides who survives in the long term. And if you consider Jewish history, it is clear that He has decided that the Jewish people have a destiny to fulfil, and therefore we have outlasted all these powerful nations (represented in the song by the animals, etc.) that have tried to destroy us.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Pesah, Educational Companion to the Questions:40
textUnits.text: Modern Jewish history reflects this same message. In the twentieth century, an enemy of the Jewish people came closer than ever before to wiping them out, yet not only did the Jewish people survive, but in fact just three years later returned to their ancestral homeland, re-established sovereignty there, and are now thriving like never before. We are part of a generation that is living the fulfilment of the message of this song.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, In a Nutshell
chapters.title: In a Nutshell

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, In a Nutshell:1
textUnits.text: Yom HaShoah is Israel’s official day of Holocaust remembrance when Jews around the world remember the six million Jewish victims of the Shoah, and the countless examples of Jewish heroism and resistance during those years. The following quotes have been taken from a series of videos recorded in 2020, in partnership with the Holocaust Educational Trust, to coincide with Yom HaShoah and the seventy-fifth anniversary of the liberation. You can watch the full video series at rabbisacks.org/holocaust.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks
chapters.title: From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:1
textUnits.text: GOD AND THE HOLOCAUST
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:2
textUnits.text: The question: Why did God allow the Holocaust to occur?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:3
textUnits.text: Rabbi Sacks’s answer: The first time I went to Auschwitz, I was simply overwhelmed. I asked, “God, where were You?” And words came into my mind…. “I was in the words ‘You shall not murder.’ I was in the words ‘You shall not oppress a stranger.’ I was in the words that were said to Kayin when he killed Hevel (the first murder in the Bible): ‘Your brother’s blood is crying to Me from the ground.’”
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:4
textUnits.text: When God speaks and human beings refuse to listen, even God is helpless in that situation. He knew that Kayin was about to kill Hevel, but He didn’t stop him. He knew Pharaoh was about to kill Israelite children. He didn’t stop it.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:5
textUnits.text: God gives us freedom and never takes it back. But He tells us how to use that freedom. And when human beings refuse to listen, even God is powerless.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:6
textUnits.text: HUMANITY AND THE HOLOCAUST
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:7
textUnits.text: The question: Do you have faith in humanity after the Holocaust?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:8
textUnits.text: Rabbi Sacks’s answer: The Holocaust represented perhaps the greatest failure humanity has ever known. It featured the combination of technical brilliance and bureaucratic efficiency, but dedicated to the most evil of all purposes. This really is the greatest failure of humanity that I can think of…. [But] there’s this very remarkable avenue called the Avenue of Righteous Gentiles, in Yad Vashem, in Jerusalem. Fourteen thousand people are honoured there, people whom any one of us would trust because they put their own lives at risk to save the lives of their neighbours and, in some cases, of strangers. These were beacons of light in the midst of one of the worst darknesses humanity has ever known, and therefore, yes, we can trust humanity if humanity shows itself capable of acting for the sake of others and taking risks to save others from death.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:9
textUnits.text: HOPE AND THE HOLOCAUST
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:10
textUnits.text: The question: Considering the devastation of the Holocaust, how can we feel hope in the Jewish future?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:11
textUnits.text: Rabbi Sacks’s answer: In the most uncanny evocation of the Holocaust, Yeḥezkel the prophet, twenty-six centuries ago, saw the Jewish people as a valley of dry bones, and God said to Yeḥezkel, “The people say our hope is lost… but it is not lost because I am going to take them out of their graves and bring them to the land of Israel.”
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:12
textUnits.text: I see three signs of hope today, and they’re remarkable.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:13
textUnits.text: Today we have Israel, we have Judaism, and we have the Jewish people, all three of them stronger than they ever were before.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:14
textUnits.text: And I don’t need any more grounds for hope than that.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:15
textUnits.text: Our hope is not destroyed.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

1. Which question do you think is harder to think about, where was God during the Holocaust or where was humanity?

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust
chapters.title: Learning Lessons from the Holocaust

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:1
textUnits.text: THE FAITH OF THE SURVIVORS
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:2
textUnits.text: The following is an excerpt from the epilogue of Rabbi Sacks’s book Future Tense.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:3
textUnits.text: It was the Holocaust survivors who taught me. I have read hundreds of books about the Shoah. I made a television programme from Auschwitz. To this day I cannot begin to imagine what they went through, how they survived the nightmare, and how they lived with the memories….
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:4
textUnits.text: The survivors I came to know in the past twenty years were astonishing in their tenacious hold on life. Perhaps it’s how they survived.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:5
textUnits.text: Some believed in God, others didn’t, but they all believed in life – not life as most of us understand it, something taken for granted, part of the background, a fact that rarely holds our attention, but life as something to fight for, as a consciously articulated value, as something of whose fragility you are constantly aware. They had, in Paul Tillich’s phrase, “the courage to be.” Slowly I began to think about another phrase, not one that exists in the traditional literature, but one that was articulated in fateful circumstances and constituted a kind of turning point in modern Jewish history: kiddush haḥayim, the sanctification of life.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:6
textUnits.text: I had expected that trauma would turn the survivors inwards, making them suspicious of, even hostile to, the wider world.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:7
textUnits.text: It didn’t, at least not those I knew, and by the time I came to know them.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:8
textUnits.text: Many of them had undertaken, fifty or more years after the event, to visit schools, talking to children, especially non-Jewish children.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:9
textUnits.text: What amazed me as I listened to them telling their stories was what they wanted to say. Cherish freedom. Understand what a gift it is to be able to walk in the open, to see a flower, open a window, breathe free air. Love others. Never hate. Practise tolerance. Stand up for others if they are being picked on, bullied, ostracised. Live each day as if it might be your last.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:10
textUnits.text: They taught the children to have faith in life. The children loved these elderly strangers from another world. I read some of their letters to them; they made me cry. Their courage kept me going through tough times. I count myself blessed to have known them.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:11
textUnits.text:
☛ REFLECT
1. Would it be understandable if the trauma of their experiences made the Holocaust survivors “suspicious of, even hostile to, the wider world”? Why?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:12
textUnits.text: 2. How was Rabbi Sacks’s experience of the survivors he met different from his expectations? What impact did that have on him?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, Learning Lessons from the Holocaust:13
textUnits.text: 3. Have you ever met or heard a talk given by a survivor? What impact did it have on you?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened
chapters.title: It Once Happened

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:1
textUnits.text: On August 11, 2017, the world’s oldest living man passed away, just a month short of his 114th birthday – making him one of the ten longest-lived men since modern record-keeping began. If you knew nothing else about him than this, you would be justified in thinking that he had led a peaceful life, spared of fear, grief, and danger.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:2
textUnits.text: The actual truth is the opposite. The man in question was Yisrael Kristal, a Holocaust survivor. Born in Poland in 1903, he survived four years in the Lodz ghetto, and was then transported to Auschwitz. In the ghetto, his two children died. In Auschwitz, his wife Chaje was killed.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:3
textUnits.text: When Auschwitz was liberated, he was a walking skeleton weighing a mere 37 kilos. He was the only member of his family to survive.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:4
textUnits.text: He was raised as a religious Jew and stayed so all his life. When the war was over and his entire world destroyed, he married another Holocaust survivor, Batsheva. They had children. They made aliya to Haifa. There he began again in the confectionery business, as he had done in Poland before the war. He made sweets and chocolate. He became an innovator.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:5
textUnits.text: If you have ever had Israeli orange peel covered in chocolate, or liqueur chocolates shaped like little bottles and covered with silver foil, you have enjoyed one of the products he originated.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:6
textUnits.text: Those who knew him said he was a man with no bitterness in his soul. He wanted people to taste sweetness.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:7
textUnits.text: In 2016, at the age of 113, he finally celebrated his bar mitzva. A hundred years earlier, this had proved impossible. By then, his mother was dead and his father was fighting in the First World War. On his bar mitzva he joked that he was the world’s oldest tefillin-wearer. He gathered his children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren under his tallit and said, “Here’s one person, and look how many people he brought to life. As we’re all standing here under my tallit, I’m thinking: Six million people. Imagine the world they could have built.”
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:8
textUnits.text:
☛ REFLECT
1. What do you find most inspiring about this story?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:9
textUnits.text: 2. What do you think was the secret of Yisrael Kristal’s long life?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, It Once Happened:10
textUnits.text: 3. We now live in an age where we have fewer and fewer survivors alive among us to tell their story. How do you think we can continue their legacy?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah
chapters.title: A Prayer for Yom HaShoah

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:1
textUnits.text: Composed by Rabbi Sacks in 2013
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:2
textUnits.text: Today, on Yom HaShoah, we remember the victims of the greatest crime of man against man –
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:3
textUnits.text: the young, the old, the innocent, the million-and-a-half children, starved, shot, given lethal injections, gassed, burned, and turned to ash, because they were deemed guilty of the crime of being different.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:4
textUnits.text: We remember what happens when hate takes hold of the human heart and turns it to stone; what happens when victims cry for help and there is no one listening;
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:5
textUnits.text: what happens when humanity fails to recognise that those who are not in our image are nonetheless in God’s image.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:6
textUnits.text: We remember and pay tribute to the survivors, who bore witness to what happened, and to the victims, so that robbed of their lives, they would not be robbed also of their deaths.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:7
textUnits.text: We remember and give thanks for the righteous of the nations who saved lives,
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:8
textUnits.text: often at risk of their own, teaching us how in the darkest night we can light a candle of hope.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:9
textUnits.text: Today, on Yom HaShoah, we call on You, Almighty God, to help us hear Your voice that says in every generation:
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:10
textUnits.text: Do not murder. Do not stand idly by the blood of your neighbour. Do not oppress the stranger.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:11
textUnits.text: We know that whilst we do not have the ability to change the past, we can change the future.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:12
textUnits.text: We know that whilst we cannot bring the dead back to life,
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:13
textUnits.text: we can ensure their memories live on and that their deaths were not in vain.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:14
textUnits.text: And so, on this Yom HaShoah, we commit ourselves to one simple act: Yizkor, Remember.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaShoah, A Prayer for Yom HaShoah:15
textUnits.text: May the souls of the victims be bound in the bond of everlasting life. Amen.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, In a Nutshell
chapters.title: In a Nutshell

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, In a Nutshell:1
textUnits.text: Yom HaZikaron (Israel’s Memorial Day) is the day on which Israel pauses to remember all those who have given up their lives fighting for and defending the State of Israel, including victims of terrorism. It falls each year on the fourth of Iyar (the day before Yom HaAtzma’ut, Israel’s Independence Day).
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks
chapters.title: From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:1
textUnits.text: FAITH IN WAR
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:2
textUnits.text: How do you live with the constant threat of violence and war? That takes faith. Israel is the people that has always been sustained by faith, faith in God, in the future, in life itself. And though Israel is a secular state, its very existence is testimony to faith: the faith of a hundred generations that Jews would one day return; the faith that led the pioneers to rebuild a land against seemingly impossible odds; the faith that after the Holocaust the Jewish people could live again; the faith that, in the face of death, continues to say: Choose life.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:3
textUnits.text: From the album “Israel – Home of Hope” produced by Rabbi Sacks
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:4
textUnits.text: FIGHTING FOR OUR VERY EXISTENCE
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:5
textUnits.text: The journey is not yet over. Israel has not yet found peace. And after four thousand years Jews still find it hard to live their faith without fear. There is only one Jewish state, a country less than one quarter of one per cent of the land mass of the Arab world – the only place on earth where Jews form a majority, the only place where they are able to do what almost every other people takes for granted: to construct a society according to their values, and to be able to defend themselves. Jews still have to fight for the right to be.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:6
textUnits.text: From the album “Israel – Home of Hope” produced by Rabbi Sacks
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:7
textUnits.text: FIGHTING FOR LIFE, FIGHTING FOR PEACE
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:8
textUnits.text: Jews fought, and never more so than in the State of Israel, with the courage that you find only in those whose ultimate aim is not victory but peace, not triumph but life. Let us acknowledge the heroes of Medinat Yisrael, the heroes not just of military battle, but also the heroes of the human spirit, who are willing to die so that we can live. They lit a flame in the Jewish heart that will never die. Let us remember them and their past, and look today at the Israel they have built: a land of freedom and energy and creativity and life.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:9
textUnits.text: From the album “Israel – Home of Hope” produced by Rabbi Sacks
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:10

1. Why do you think the State of Israel chose to remember its fallen on the day before Yom HaAtzma’ut, when it celebrates its independence?

textUnits.text: 2. How have we benefitted from the sacrifice of those who have given their lives for the State of Israel?

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:13
textUnits.text: CARRYING THE PAST, TURNING DEATH INTO LIFE
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:14
textUnits.text: At the end of the book of Bereshit, Yosef makes one deeply poignant request: Though I will die in exile, God will bring you back to the land, and when He does so, “vehaalitem et atzmotai mizeh,” “carry my bones” with you.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:15
textUnits.text: Moshe smashed the first set of tablets given to him by God at Mount Sinai, but the Israelites carried them in the Ark, together with the second set: the new tablets and the fragments of the old.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:16
textUnits.text: And so it has been throughout Jewish history; we carry with us all the fragments of our people’s past, the broken lives, the anguished deaths. For we refuse to let their deaths be in vain. Our past lives on in us as we continue the Jewish journey to the future, to hope, and to life.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:17
textUnits.text: On Yom HaZikaron we remember the members of the Israel Defense Forces who fell in action, and also all those killed by terrorist attacks in Israel. What our enemies killed, we keep alive in the only way we can: in our minds, our memories, and in our land, the State of Israel.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:18
textUnits.text: There are cultures that forget the past and there are those that are held captive by the past. We do neither. We carry the past with us for as long as the Jewish people exist, as Moshe carried the bones of Yosef, and as the Levites carried the fragments of the shattered tablets of stone.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:19
textUnits.text: Those fragments of memory, of those no longer with us, help make us who we are. We live for what they died for, by walking tall as Jews, showing we are not afraid, refusing to be intimidated by the anti-Semitism that has returned, or the sustained assault on Israel.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:20
textUnits.text: On Yom HaZikaron, as we remember those who have fallen or been killed in defence of the State of Israel, we say to the souls of those lost: We will never forget you. We will never cease to mourn you. We will never let you down.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.title: It Once Happened

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:1
textUnits.text: I met Yoni Jesner in Jerusalem in January 2002. He was nineteen years old, just beginning his second year in yeshiva. We had brought together a group of three hundred British students, but he stood out among them as a leader, a young man with quiet inner strength and a sense of humour that drew people to him and brought out the best in them. I knew of his reputation from the community in Glasgow where he had grown up. Already he was something of a legend. He worked with the young and the old, he took children’s services in the synagogue, taught in its classes, ran the local youth group, and was a volunteer in the burial society, helping prepare the dead for burial with dignity. A brilliant student, he had decided to become a doctor and already had a place at medical school. His first priority was to dedicate his life to saving lives. Like many others in Jewish history, he saw medicine as a religious vocation.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:2
textUnits.text: Yoni was travelling on the number 4 bus in Tel Aviv on September 19, 2002, when the suicide bomber detonated his belt. Ari, his brother in London, caught the next flight to Israel. Yoni Jesner, of blessed memory, was a remarkable young man whose death at the hands of a suicide bomber devastated all who knew him.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:3
textUnits.text: It turned out, though, that Yoni had a last and yet more deeply moving message for us. After consulting Yoni’s rabbi, his family came to a decision. Yoni had wanted to save lives. They would donate his organs. Among those whose lives were transformed was Yasmin Abu Ramila, a seven-year-old Palestinian girl from East Jerusalem who had been on dialysis for two years awaiting a compatible transplant. This is moral greatness of a high order – to create life out of death and turn a potential enemy into a friend. It takes exceptional courage to come to such a decision in the midst of grief, but acts like these are fragments of redemption.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:4
textUnits.text: A people is as great as its ideals, and Yoni lived those ideals to the limit. We will not forget him. We will cherish his memory as a blessing and inspiration.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:5
textUnits.text: To Heal a Fractured World, 208–209
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:6
textUnits.text: A MESSAGE TO HONOUR THE LIVES AND MEMORIES OF OUR FALLEN LONE SOLDIERS
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:7
textUnits.text: We remember the courage and the mesirat nefesh (self-sacrifice), the dedication and the bravery, of Israel’s Ḥayalim bodedim (lone soldiers), especially those who gave their lives defending Medinat Yisrael and am Yisrael.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:8
textUnits.text: We think of them as living examples of what it is to fight for the freedom of our people, and their safety, in the land of our beginnings, so that never again would am Yisrael be dependent on the goodwill of the nations.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:9
textUnits.text: Never again would we have to suffer the two thousand years of persecution of the centuries that preceded the birth of the State of Israel. These are among the great heroes of our people.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:10
textUnits.text: Let us honour the memory of those who died. Let us salute the example of those who live. And let us pray to Hashem to bless the State of Israel, the people of Israel, and the Defense Forces of Israel, and may He give all of us the blessing of health, and strength, and peace.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaZikaron, It Once Happened:11
textUnits.text: Amen.

textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.text: Rabbi Sacks shared this message in 2020 to honour the lives and memories of our fallen lone soldiers at the annual Yom HaZikaron ceremony of the Lone Soldier Center in Memory of Michael Levin.

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, Yom HaAtzma'ut in a Nutshell
chapters.title: Yom HaAtzma'ut in a Nutshell

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, Yom HaAtzma'ut in a Nutshell:1
textUnits.text: The State of Israel came into existence on May 14, 1948, as David Ben-Gurion, the first prime minister of Israel, read the Declaration of Independence in Tel Aviv on behalf of the provisional government. The Hebrew date was the fifth day of the month of Iyar 5708, and every year on this day we celebrate Yom HaAtzma’ut, Israel’s Independence Day. In Israel, the day is celebrated with an official ceremony on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem, nationwide street parties at night, and hiking and picnicking during the day. Religious Jews conduct special prayer services to acknowledge and give thanks to God for His role in the miraculous story of the establishment and continued existence of the State of Israel.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

chapters.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks
chapters.title: From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:1
textUnits.text: THE MIRACLE OF THE STATE OF ISRAEL
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:2
textUnits.text: The creation of the State of Israel was fraught with difficulty. Despite the Balfour Declaration of 1917, in which Britain, the new mandatory power in Palestine, promised Jews a national home, there was intense opposition – from the Arab world, from other international forces, from politicians in Britain, and at times from Jews themselves. For thirty years, various compromises were proposed, all accepted by Jews and rejected by their opponents. On the day the State of Israel was proclaimed, the country was attacked on all fronts by its neighbours. Since then, it has lived under constant threat of war, violence, terror, and delegitimisation. Yet Israel has achieved wondrous things.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:3
textUnits.text: Through it, Hebrew, the language of the Bible, was reborn as a living tongue. Jewish communities under threat have been rescued, including those like the Jews of Ethiopia who had little contact with other Jews for centuries. Jews have come to Israel from over a hundred countries, representing the entire lexicon of cultural diversity. A desolate landscape has bloomed again. Jerusalem has been rebuilt. The world of Torah scholarship, devastated by the Holocaust, has been revived and the sound of learning echoes throughout the land. Economically, politically, socially, and culturally, Israel’s achievements are unmatched by any country of its age and size. The Sages said that, at the crossing of the Red Sea, the simplest Jew saw miracles that the greatest of later prophets were not destined to see. That, surely, was the privilege of those who witnessed Israel’s rebirth and youth. The Messiah has not come. Israel is not yet at peace. The Temple has not been rebuilt. Our time is not yet redemption. Yet many of the prayers of two thousand years have been answered. No one, reviewing this singular history, can doubt that faith makes a difference, that a nation’s history is shaped by what it believes.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:4
textUnits.text: Many of the heroes and pioneers of the return to Zion were not “spiritual,” nor did they observe many of the commandments. But the vision of the prophets and the covenant of Jewish history flowed through their veins. God works through people; sometimes, so the prophets taught, without their conscious knowledge and consent. It is difficult to reflect deeply on the rebirth of Israel without sensing the touch of heaven in the minds of men and women, leading them to play their parts in a drama so much greater than any individual could have executed, even conceived.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:5
textUnits.text: Who, then, wrote the script of the Jewish drama? God or the Jewish people? Or was it, as the Sages taught, an inextricable combination of both: God as He was heard by the people, and the people as they responded to God? Isaac Bashevis Singer came close when he said, “God is a writer and we are both the heroes and the readers.”
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:6
textUnits.text: The Jonathan Sacks Haggada, 66–68
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:7
textUnits.text: WHY A LAND?
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:8
textUnits.text: [Jewish] destiny was to create a society that would honour the proposition that we are all created in the image and likeness of God. It would be a place in which the freedom of some would not lead to the enslavement of others.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:9
textUnits.text: Judaism is the code of a self-governing society. We tend to forget this, since Jews have lived in dispersion for two thousand years, without the sovereign power to govern themselves, and because modern Israel is a secular state.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:10
textUnits.text: Because Judaism is the code of a society, it is also about the social virtues: righteousness (tzedek/tzedaka), justice (mishpat), loving-kindness (Ḥesed), and compassion (raḥamim). These structure the template of biblical law, which covers all aspects of the life of society, its economy, its welfare systems, its education, family life, employer-employee relations, the protection of the environment, and so on.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:11
textUnits.text: None of this is possible without a land. Judaism is the constitution of a self-governing nation, the architectonics of a society dedicated to the service of God in freedom and dignity. Without a land and state, Judaism is a shadow of itself. In exile, God might still live in the hearts of Jews but not in the public square, in the justice of the courts, the morality of the economy, and the humanitarianism of everyday life.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:12
textUnits.text: Jews have lived in almost every country under the sun. In four thousand years, only in Israel have they been a free, self-governing people. Only in Israel are they able, if they so choose, to construct an agriculture, a medical system, an economic infrastructure in the spirit of the Torah and its concern for freedom, justice, and the sanctity of life. Only in Israel can Jews today speak the Hebrew of the Bible as the language of everyday speech. Only in Israel can they live Jewish time within a calendar structured according to the rhythms of the Jewish year. Only in Israel can Jews live Judaism in anything other than an edited edition. In Israel, and only there, Jews can walk where the prophets walked, climb the mountains Avraham climbed, lift their eyes to the hills that David saw, and continue the story their ancestors began.
textUnits.version: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023
textUnits.attribution: Sefaria edition: Ceremony & Celebration Family Edition, Maggid Books, 2023

textUnits.ref: Ceremony and Celebration Family Edition, The Hagim, Yom HaAtzma'ut, From the Thought of Rabbi Sacks:13
textUnits.text: Future Tense, 135–136
